dev.tanrei.vocabulary.rationale: One product tells people how to do something in an order that matters — install, configure, build, check — and wants that procedure told apart from a list that merely happens to be numbered: each step's number easy to find again after looking away at a terminal, each step's extent plain when it holds several blocks, and the steps read as one sequence. It writes a short one in a panel at the interface's text size and a long one on a page at the reading size.

dev.tanrei.llm.usage: Everything a set of steps reads: per size, the marker's minimum height, the text style of its number, of a step's title and of a step's body; the marker's inline padding, corners and edge; the space between the marker and the step's content; the connector's color, thickness and its distance from the markers it joins; the space between two steps, between a title and its body, and between the blocks of one body.
rules: Steps are a procedure to read: things done in order, each step a number, an optional title and a body. They are an ordered list and nothing else: no step is current, done or failed, and nothing in them is pressed.

Progress through a flow the person is in (a checkout, a setup wizard: a current step, completed steps, a step with an error, steps that are pressed to go back) is not this component. Do not mark a step as done or current by restyling a marker.

A list that is numbered only so its items can be referred to, or whose items are a phrase each, is an ordered list of prose. Use steps where the order is the point and a reader will work through them.
A step's body is the product's content, laid out as prose: paragraphs, a code block, a table, tabs. Sub-steps are an ordered list inside the body; do not nest steps in steps.
Steps bring no text color and no fill: the number, the title and the body take the content color of the surface they sit on. The ring and the connector are the system's one hairline.
Use start to continue a procedure that a note or a heading interrupts; never write numbers into the titles.
Use size large on a page whose purpose is reading, with the prose around it; medium among controls.
marker.height is a minimum: a marker grows with enlarged text and widens for a long number.
Restyle through these tokens in a layer; never draw a numbered circle or a guide line by hand.

height.$description: The marker's minimum height, and its minimum width, per size: two more than one line of the body's text at that size (22 and 26 in the default system), so the ring stands a little outside the line it is centred on and one-line steps never touch. A minimum: the marker grows with its number's text.

padding-inline.$description: The least room between the marker's edge and its number at the start and the end. With it a number of one or two digits keeps the marker a circle in the default system; a longer one (a procedure continued at 100) widens it into a pill.

dev.tanrei.vocabulary.rationale: One product numbers a short procedure 1 to 5 and continues a long one past 9 and past 99; the marker has to hold each without its number touching the ring.

shape.$description: The marker's corners: a circle in the default system, and a pill where the number widens it. Never larger than half the marker's height.

color.$description: The ring: the system's one hairline. Decorative — the number inside it is what is read — so it is not held to a contrast.

width.$description: The ring's width, drawn inside the marker's size.

typescale.$description: The text style of the number, per size: a label style, a step under the body's size at medium and at the body's size at large, so the number is a mark beside the text and never louder than it.

gap.$description: The space between the marker's column and the step's content. Every step's content begins at the same edge: the widest marker's width and this gap from the steps' start edge.

dev.tanrei.vocabulary.rationale: One product shows that its steps are one sequence, and where a step with several blocks ends, by a line from each marker to the next; a product with a plainer manner draws none, which is a thickness of zero.

color.$description: The line that joins a marker to the next: the system's one hairline, the ring's color. Decorative.

thickness.$description: The connector's thickness. Zero draws no connector.

gap.$description: The space the connector keeps from the marker above it and from the marker below it, so the line and the rings are read as separate marks.

The space between the end of one step and the beginning of the next: the space prose puts between two blocks in the default system, so a step is a block of the text it sits in, and twice the space between the blocks inside one step.

dev.tanrei.vocabulary.rationale: One product names the steps of a long procedure ("Install", "Configure") so that a reader finds the step they stopped at, and leaves the three lines of a short one unnamed.

typescale.$description: The text style of a step's title, per size: the heading role whose size is the body's at that size, so a title is told from the body by its weight and not by being larger.

gap.$description: The space between a step's title and its body.

typescale.$description: The text style a step's body takes where nothing inside it sets another, per size: the running text of prose at the same size.

gap.$description: The space between two blocks of one step's body (a paragraph and the code block it introduces): what prose puts between the blocks nested in a list item in the default system, and half the space between two steps, so what belongs to one step is closer together than two steps are.
